name: Leg press
purpose: Builds the big muscles of your legs and bum with a fixed path, so you can push hard without worrying about balance.
cue: Push through your whole foot, stop short of locking your knees.
setup: Sit with your back and head flat against the pad.
Put your feet on the platform about shoulder-width apart, in the middle of the plate.
Hold the side handles and release the safety catches.
execution: Lower the platform slowly by bending your knees toward your chest.
Go down until your knees are at about a right angle, or just before your lower back starts to lift off the pad.
Push the platform away through your whole foot until your legs are almost straight.
Keep your knees pointing the same way as your toes the whole time.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower the weight, breathe out as you push or pull it.
feelItIn: The front of your thighs and your glutes.
commonMistakes: Locking the knees hard at the top
Letting the lower back curl off the pad at the bottom
safety: Always re-engage the safety catches before getting out. Never fully lock your knees under load.

name: Chest press machine
purpose: Builds your chest, front shoulders and triceps on a guided path, the safest way to learn pressing.
cue: Shoulder blades back and down, press out without shrugging.
setup: Adjust the seat so the handles line up with the middle of your chest.
Sit tall with your back against the pad and feet flat on the floor.
Grab the handles with your wrists straight.
execution: Squeeze your shoulder blades together and keep them there.
Press the handles forward until your arms are straight but not locked.
Slowly let the handles come back until you feel a stretch across your chest.
Keep your elbows a little below shoulder height, not flared straight out.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower the weight, breathe out as you push or pull it.
feelItIn: Across your chest, with some work in the front of your shoulders and the back of your arms.
commonMistakes: Seat too low or too high
Shoulders rolling forward at the end of the press
Letting the weight stack slam between reps
Flaring elbows straight out to the sides

name: Lat pulldown
purpose: Builds the wide muscles of your back (the ones that make a V-shape) and teaches the pull-up motion.
cue: Pull your elbows down to your back pockets, chest up.
setup: Set the thigh pad so your legs are locked in snugly.
Grab the bar a bit wider than shoulder-width with palms facing away.
Sit down with arms straight overhead and lean back just slightly.
execution: Start by pulling your shoulders down away from your ears.
Pull the bar down to your upper chest, driving your elbows down and slightly back.
Pause briefly with your chest up to meet the bar.
Let the bar rise slowly until your arms are straight again.
breathing: Breathe out as you pull down, breathe in as the bar goes back up.
feelItIn: The sides of your back under your armpits, plus your biceps.
commonMistakes: Leaning way back and turning it into a row
Pulling the bar behind your neck
Letting the bar yank your arms up fast

name: Seated leg curl
purpose: Strengthens the back of your thighs, which protects your knees and balances all the cycling you do.
cue: Curl your heels down and under, hips stay glued to the seat.
setup: Sit with the back of your knees at the edge of the seat and knees lined up with the machine's pivot point.
Put the lower pad just above your heels and lower the thigh pad onto your legs.
Hold the handles.
execution: Curl your heels down and back as far as you comfortably can.
Squeeze the back of your thighs for a moment.
Let the pad come back up slowly until your legs are nearly straight.
breathing: Breathe out as you curl, in as you return.
feelItIn: The back of your thighs.
commonMistakes: Lifting your hips off the seat
Letting the weight snap back up

name: Shoulder press machine
purpose: Builds strong, rounder shoulders and teaches the overhead press on a guided path.
cue: Ribs down, press straight up, don't shrug.
setup: Set the seat so the handles start at about shoulder height.
Sit tall with your back against the pad.
Grip the handles with wrists straight above your elbows.
execution: Press the handles up until your arms are nearly straight.
Keep your lower back on the pad; don't arch.
Lower slowly back to shoulder height.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower the weight, breathe out as you push or pull it.
feelItIn: The front and sides of your shoulders, and the back of your arms.
commonMistakes: Arching your lower back to push more
Shrugging the shoulders up to your ears
Seat set so low the handles start below your chin

name: Plank
purpose: Teaches your midsection to hold your spine still, which is what your core really does when you lift heavy.
cue: Squeeze your glutes, push the floor away, body in a straight line.
setup: Lie face down and prop yourself on your forearms, elbows under your shoulders.
Lift your hips so your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
execution: Squeeze your glutes and tighten your stomach.
Push your forearms into the floor so your upper back stays wide.
Hold the position, breathing slowly. Stop when your hips start to sag.
breathing: Breathe slowly and shallowly through your nose; don't hold your breath.
feelItIn: Your stomach working hard to keep your hips from dropping.
commonMistakes: Bum sticking up in the air
Looking up and straining your neck

name: Goblet squat
purpose: The easiest way to learn the squat: holding the weight in front keeps you upright and balanced.
cue: Elbows down, chest up, sit between your heels.
setup: Hold one dumbbell vertically against your chest, both hands cupping the top end.
Stand with feet a little wider than shoulder-width, toes turned out slightly.
execution: Take a breath and brace your stomach.
Sit down between your heels, keeping your chest up and the dumbbell close.
Go down until your hips are at least level with your knees (deeper is fine if your back stays flat).
Drive up through your whole foot to stand tall.
breathing: Take a deep breath into your belly and tighten your stomach as if bracing for a poke, then hold it through the hard part of the rep. Breathe out at the top.
feelItIn: The front of your thighs and your glutes. Your upper back works to hold the weight.
commonMistakes: Knees caving in on the way up
Leaning forward and letting the dumbbell drift away

name: Seated cable row
purpose: Builds the middle of your back for better posture and balances all the pushing exercises.
cue: Chest tall, pull the handle to your belly button, squeeze your shoulder blades.
setup: Attach a close-grip (V) handle. Sit with your feet on the platform, knees slightly bent.
Grab the handle and sit tall with your arms straight and back flat.
execution: Pull the handle toward your belly button, driving your elbows back close to your sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end.
Let your arms straighten slowly, feeling a stretch across your upper back, without rounding your lower back.
breathing: Breathe out as you pull, in as you return.
feelItIn: Between and around your shoulder blades.
commonMistakes: Rocking your whole body back and forth
Rounding your lower back on the return

name: Incline dumbbell press
purpose: Builds your upper chest and front shoulders, the part that makes the chest look full in a T-shirt.
cue: Shoulder blades pinned, lower to the upper chest, press up and slightly in.
setup: Set the bench to a low incline (about 30°).
Sit with a dumbbell on each thigh, then lie back and bring them up to your shoulders as you go.
Plant your feet and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
execution: Press the dumbbells up over your upper chest until your arms are straight.
Lower them slowly to the sides of your upper chest, elbows at about 45° from your body.
Feel a stretch in your chest at the bottom, then press up again.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower the weight, breathe out as you push or pull it.
feelItIn: Your upper chest and the front of your shoulders.
commonMistakes: Bench too steep (turns it into a shoulder press)
Bouncing the weights at the bottom
Lifting your bum off the bench
safety: To finish, bring the dumbbells to your chest and sit up with them, or lower them to the floor beside you with control. Never drop them over your face.

name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift
purpose: Teaches the hip hinge, the most important movement for a strong back, glutes and hamstrings.
cue: Push your hips back, keep the dumbbells close, back flat.
setup: Stand with feet hip-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs.
Unlock your knees slightly and pull your shoulders back.
execution: Push your hips back as if closing a door behind you with your bum.
Let the dumbbells slide down the front of your legs, keeping your back flat.
Stop when you feel a strong stretch in the back of your thighs (usually around mid-shin).
Drive your hips forward to stand up, squeezing your glutes at the top.
breathing: Take a deep breath into your belly and tighten your stomach as if bracing for a poke, then hold it through the hard part of the rep. Breathe out at the top.
feelItIn: A big stretch in the back of your thighs, then your glutes working to stand up.
commonMistakes: Rounding your back to reach lower
Bending the knees a lot so it becomes a squat
Letting the dumbbells drift away from your legs
safety: If you feel it in your lower back rather than your hamstrings, go lighter and shorten the range.

name: Dumbbell curl
purpose: Builds the biceps on the front of your upper arm.
cue: Elbows pinned to your sides, curl up, lower slowly.
setup: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, arms by your sides, palms facing forward.
execution: Curl the dumbbells up by bending at the elbows only.
Squeeze at the top without letting your elbows drift forward.
Lower slowly until your arms are fully straight.
breathing: Breathe out as you curl, in as you lower.
feelItIn: The front of your upper arms.
commonMistakes: Swinging your body to lift the weight
Cutting the bottom half of the rep short

name: Cable triceps pushdown
purpose: Builds the triceps on the back of your arm, which make up most of your upper-arm size.
cue: Elbows glued to your sides, push down until your arms are straight.
setup: Attach a straight bar or rope to a high cable.
Stand close, grab it with palms down, elbows tucked at your sides.
execution: Push the handle down until your arms are fully straight.
Squeeze the back of your arms for a second.
Let it come back up until your forearms are about parallel to the floor, elbows staying put.
breathing: Breathe out as you push down, in as you return.
feelItIn: The back of your upper arms.
commonMistakes: Leaning over and using body weight
Letting the handle rise to your face

name: Dead bug
purpose: A gentle but tough core exercise that teaches you to keep your lower back still while your arms and legs move.
cue: Lower back pressed into the floor, move slowly, opposite arm and leg.
setup: Lie on your back with arms pointing to the ceiling.
Lift your legs so your knees are bent at 90°, right above your hips.
Press your lower back flat into the floor.
execution: Slowly lower one arm behind your head and the opposite leg toward the floor at the same time.
Stop just before your lower back starts to lift.
Bring them back and switch sides. Each side counts as one rep.
breathing: Breathe out slowly as you extend, in as you return.
feelItIn: Deep in your stomach, holding your lower back down.
commonMistakes: Lower back arching off the floor

name: Barbell back squat
purpose: The king of leg exercises: builds your legs, glutes and whole-body strength like nothing else.
cue: Big breath, brace, sit down between your heels, drive up.
setup: Set the bar in the rack at mid-chest height and the safety pins just below how low you'll squat.
Step under the bar and rest it on the meaty part of your upper back (not your neck). Grip it just outside your shoulders.
Stand up to lift it off, take two or three small steps back, feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out.
execution: Take a big breath into your belly and brace.
Bend your hips and knees together and sit down between your heels, knees following your toes.
Go down until your hip crease is at least level with the top of your knees, back flat.
Drive up through your whole foot, chest up, until you're standing tall. Breathe, re-brace, repeat.
breathing: Take a deep breath into your belly and tighten your stomach as if bracing for a poke, then hold it through the hard part of the rep. Breathe out at the top.
feelItIn: Your thighs and glutes, with your whole midsection working hard to stay tight.
commonMistakes: Heels lifting or weight shifting to the toes
Chest dropping so the squat turns into a good-morning
safety: Always squat inside the rack with the safety pins set. If a rep fails, sit down onto the pins and step out.

name: Smith machine squat
purpose: A guided version of the squat: the bar runs on rails, so it's a good first step toward the free barbell.
cue: Feet slightly in front of the bar, sit down and back, drive up.
setup: Set the bar at mid-chest height and the safety stops just below your bottom position.
Get under the bar so it rests on your upper back, feet shoulder-width and a little in front of the bar.
Twist the bar to unhook it.
execution: Brace and sit down until your thighs are about level with the floor.
Drive up through your whole foot to stand tall.
Twist the bar back onto the hooks when you're done.
breathing: Take a deep breath into your belly and tighten your stomach as if bracing for a poke, then hold it through the hard part of the rep. Breathe out at the top.
feelItIn: Your thighs and glutes.
commonMistakes: Feet directly under the bar (puts stress on the knees)
safety: Bar weights differ between Smith machines (some are counter-balanced). Log the same way every time and progress from there.

name: Dumbbell bench press
purpose: Builds your chest, shoulders and triceps; each arm works on its own, which evens out weak sides.
cue: Shoulder blades pinned, lower to mid-chest, elbows at 45°.
setup: Sit on a flat bench with the dumbbells on your thighs.
Lie back and use your knees to help bring the dumbbells up beside your chest.
Plant your feet, squeeze your shoulder blades together and down.
execution: Press the dumbbells up over your chest until your arms are straight.
Lower them slowly to the sides of your mid-chest, elbows at about 45° from your body.
Feel a stretch across your chest, then press back up.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower the weight, breathe out as you push or pull it.
feelItIn: Across your chest and in the back of your arms.
commonMistakes: Elbows flared straight out to the sides
Dropping the weights at the end
safety: To finish, bring the dumbbells to your chest, then roll up to sitting with them on your thighs.

name: Chest-supported dumbbell row
purpose: Builds your upper back with your chest resting on a bench, so your lower back gets a break.
cue: Chest on the pad, pull elbows back toward your hips, squeeze.
setup: Set a bench to about 30–45° and lie face down on it, chest at the top edge.
Let a dumbbell hang straight down in each hand, palms facing each other.
execution: Pull the dumbbells up and back toward your hips, elbows close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
breathing: Breathe out as you pull, in as you lower.
feelItIn: Your upper back and the back of your shoulders.
commonMistakes: Lifting your chest off the bench to cheat
Using a weight so heavy the reps get short

name: Dumbbell shoulder press
purpose: Builds strong, broad shoulders; free weights also train the small stabilising muscles.
cue: Ribs down, press up and slightly in, don't arch.
setup: Set a bench upright (or nearly). Sit with a dumbbell on each thigh.
Kick them up one at a time to shoulder height, palms facing forward.
execution: Press the dumbbells up until your arms are straight overhead.
Lower slowly back to shoulder height.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower the weight, breathe out as you push or pull it.
feelItIn: The front and sides of your shoulders and the back of your arms.
commonMistakes: Banging the dumbbells together at the top

name: Cable face pull
purpose: Strengthens the back of your shoulders and upper back, which protects your shoulders and improves posture.
cue: Pull the rope to your eyes, hands apart, elbows high.
setup: Set a rope on a cable at about face height.
Grab the ends with palms facing down and step back until your arms are straight.
execution: Pull the rope toward your eyes, pulling the ends apart as you go.
Finish with your hands beside your ears and elbows high, like a double-biceps pose.
Return slowly.
breathing: Breathe out as you pull, in as you return.
feelItIn: The back of your shoulders and between your shoulder blades.
commonMistakes: Going too heavy and leaning back
Pulling to the chest instead of the face

name: Pallof press
purpose: Trains your core to resist twisting, which makes you steadier in every other lift.
cue: Stand tall, press straight out, don't let the cable turn you.
setup: Set a cable handle at chest height. Stand side-on to the machine, a big step away.
Hold the handle with both hands at your chest, feet shoulder-width.
execution: Press the handle straight out in front of your chest.
Hold for a second while the cable tries to twist you toward it.
Bring it back to your chest. Do all reps, then turn around for the other side.
breathing: Breathe out as you press, in as you return.
feelItIn: The sides of your stomach.

name: Barbell Romanian deadlift
purpose: The barbell version of the hip hinge: builds powerful hamstrings, glutes and a strong back.
cue: Hips back, bar slides down your thighs, back flat.
setup: Set the bar in a rack at mid-thigh height (or deadlift it from the floor).
Grip it just outside your thighs, stand tall, shoulders back.
execution: Unlock your knees and push your hips back.
Slide the bar down your thighs, keeping it touching your legs and your back flat.
Stop just below the knees, or when your hamstrings stop you.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall, squeezing your glutes.
breathing: Take a deep breath into your belly and tighten your stomach as if bracing for a poke, then hold it through the hard part of the rep. Breathe out at the top.
feelItIn: A deep stretch in your hamstrings and hard work in your glutes.
commonMistakes: Bar drifting away from the legs
safety: Your lower back should feel worked, never strained. If it does, go lighter and shorten the range.

name: Assisted pull-up
purpose: A pull-up with help from a machine or band, so you can build toward doing them on your own.
cue: Chest up to the bar, pull your elbows down to your ribs.
setup: On an assisted pull-up machine, choose the help amount (more weight = more help).
Kneel or stand on the pad and grab the handles a bit wider than your shoulders.
No machine? Loop a resistance band over the bar and put a knee or foot in it.
execution: Hang with arms straight, then pull your shoulders down.
Pull yourself up until your chin is over the bar, elbows driving down.
Lower slowly all the way until your arms are straight.
breathing: Breathe out as you pull up, in as you lower.
feelItIn: The sides of your back and your biceps.
commonMistakes: Half reps that don't fully straighten the arms
safety: On the machine, the number is help, so a lower number means you're stronger.

name: Split squat
purpose: Trains one leg at a time for balance and evens out differences between your legs; great for cycling too.
cue: Drop your back knee straight down, front foot flat.
setup: Stand in a long stride, one foot forward and one back, feet hip-width apart (like on train tracks, not a tightrope).
Hold a dumbbell in each hand, or none to start. Lift your back heel.
execution: Lower your back knee straight down toward the floor.
Stop just before it touches; your front shin should be fairly upright.
Push through your front foot to come back up. Do all reps on one leg, then switch.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower the weight, breathe out as you push or pull it.
feelItIn: The front thigh and glute of your front leg.
commonMistakes: Stance too short so the front knee shoots forward
Feet in one line, making it wobbly

name: Farmer carry
purpose: Walking with heavy dumbbells: builds grip, traps and a rock-solid core. Simple and very effective.
cue: Stand tall, shoulders back, walk with short steady steps.
setup: Put two heavy dumbbells by your feet.
Squat down, grab them and stand up tall.
execution: Walk with short, even steps, keeping your shoulders back and chest up.
Keep your stomach tight and don't let the weights swing.
Walk for the target time, turning around as needed, then put them down carefully.
breathing: Breathe steadily; don't hold your breath.
feelItIn: Your grip, shoulders and the whole trunk.
commonMistakes: Dropping the weights at the end

name: One-arm dumbbell row
purpose: Builds the back one side at a time, with a big stretch and a strong squeeze.
cue: Flat back, pull the dumbbell to your hip.
setup: Put one knee and the same-side hand on a flat bench, back flat like a table.
Hold a dumbbell in the other hand, arm hanging straight down.
execution: Pull the dumbbell up toward your hip, elbow close to your body.
Squeeze your back at the top, then lower slowly until your arm is straight.
Do all reps on one side, then switch.
breathing: Breathe out as you pull, in as you lower.
feelItIn: The side of your back and behind your shoulder.
commonMistakes: Twisting your torso to lift the weight
Pulling toward the chest instead of the hip

name: Back extension
purpose: Strengthens your glutes, hamstrings and lower back in a safe, controlled way.
cue: Hinge at the hips, rise until your body is straight, squeeze your glutes.
setup: Set the 45° back-extension bench so the pad sits just below your hip bones.
Lock your heels under the foot pads, cross your arms on your chest.
execution: Lower your upper body by bending at the hips, keeping your back flat.
Rise back up until your body is in a straight line, squeezing your glutes.
Don't arch past straight. To make it harder, hold a weight plate on your chest.
breathing: Breathe in on the way down, out on the way up.
feelItIn: Your glutes and hamstrings, with your lower back holding steady.
commonMistakes: Pad too high so you can't bend at the hips

name: Side plank
purpose: Strengthens the sides of your core, which keeps your hips level when walking, cycling and carrying.
cue: Hips high, body in one straight line.
setup: Lie on your side, propped on your forearm with your elbow under your shoulder.
Stack your feet (or stagger them for balance).
execution: Lift your hips until your body is straight from head to feet.
Hold, breathing slowly. Do one side, then the other.
breathing: Breathe slowly and steadily.
feelItIn: The side of your waist closest to the floor.
commonMistakes: Shoulder shrugged up to the ear

name: Barbell bench press
purpose: The classic upper-body strength lift: builds chest, shoulders and triceps.
cue: Shoulder blades pinned, bar to lower chest, press back over your shoulders.
setup: Lie on the bench with your eyes directly under the bar. Set the safety arms just below chest height.
Grip the bar a little wider than shoulder-width, wrists straight.
Plant your feet, squeeze your shoulder blades together and down, and unrack the bar over your shoulders.
execution: Lower the bar under control to your lower chest, elbows at about 45°.
Touch lightly (no bounce), then press back up and slightly back toward your face.
Finish with arms straight and the bar over your shoulders.
breathing: Breathe in and hold at the top, lower and press, breathe out at the top.
feelItIn: Across your chest and the back of your arms.
commonMistakes: Bouncing the bar off your chest
safety: Always use the safety arms or a spotter. Never bench with collars off if you might need to tilt the bar to escape; use the safeties instead.

name: Deadlift
purpose: Lifts a barbell from the floor: builds strength through your whole back side, from grip to calves.
cue: Bar over mid-foot, brace, push the floor away, bar stays touching your legs.
setup: Stand with the bar over the middle of your feet, feet hip-width apart.
Bend down and grip the bar just outside your legs.
Bend your knees until your shins touch the bar. Chest up, back flat, arms straight.
execution: Take a big breath and brace. Pull the slack out of the bar (you'll hear a click).
Push the floor away with your legs; hips and shoulders rise together.
Once the bar passes your knees, drive your hips forward to stand tall.
Lower it by pushing your hips back first, then bending your knees once it passes them.
breathing: Take a deep breath into your belly and tighten your stomach as if bracing for a poke, then hold it through the hard part of the rep. Breathe out at the top.
feelItIn: Glutes, hamstrings and your whole back working to stay flat.
commonMistakes: Bar starting too far in front of the feet
Jerking the bar off the floor
Leaning far back at the top
safety: If you can't keep your back flat, the weight is too heavy. Use bumper plates or blocks if you lack full-size plates.

name: Trap-bar deadlift
purpose: A deadlift standing inside a hexagon bar. Easier on the back and easier to learn, but still great for strength.
cue: Stand in the middle, chest up, push the floor away.
setup: Stand in the centre of the trap bar, feet hip-width apart.
Squat down and grip the handles in the middle. Chest up, back flat.
execution: Brace and push the floor away to stand up tall.
Lower by sitting your hips back and down under control.
breathing: Take a deep breath into your belly and tighten your stomach as if bracing for a poke, then hold it through the hard part of the rep. Breathe out at the top.
feelItIn: Your thighs, glutes and back.
commonMistakes: Gripping off-centre so the bar tips

name: Overhead press
purpose: Pressing a barbell overhead standing up: builds big, strong shoulders and a stable core.
cue: Squeeze glutes, ribs down, press straight up, head through at the top.
setup: Set the bar in the rack at upper-chest height. Grip it just outside your shoulders.
Unrack it so it rests on the front of your shoulders, elbows slightly in front of the bar.
Stand with feet hip-width, squeeze your glutes and stomach.
execution: Press the bar straight up, moving your head back slightly to let it pass.
Once it's past your forehead, push your head forward 'through the window' so the bar ends over your mid-foot.
Lower it under control back to your shoulders.
breathing: Take a deep breath into your belly and tighten your stomach as if bracing for a poke, then hold it through the hard part of the rep. Breathe out at the top.
feelItIn: Your shoulders and the back of your arms; your core keeps you from leaning back.
commonMistakes: Leaning back a lot (turning it into a standing bench press)
Pressing the bar forward instead of straight up

name: Barbell row
purpose: Rowing a barbell while bent over: builds a thick, strong back.
cue: Hinge to about 45°, pull the bar to your lower ribs, back flat.
setup: Hold the bar with an overhand grip just outside your thighs.
Hinge forward from the hips to about 45°, knees softly bent, back flat.
execution: Pull the bar to your lower ribs, driving your elbows back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
Lower until your arms are straight, staying in the bent-over position.
breathing: Breathe out as you pull, in as you lower.
feelItIn: Your upper and mid back; your hamstrings and lower back hold you in position.
commonMistakes: Standing up more with each rep
Jerking the weight with your hips

name: Pull-up
purpose: Pulling your own body up to a bar: one of the best back builders and a real milestone of strength.
cue: Shoulders down first, then pull your chest toward the bar.
setup: Grab the bar with palms facing away, a bit wider than your shoulders.
Hang with arms straight and feet off the floor (bend your knees if needed).
execution: Pull your shoulders down away from your ears.
Pull yourself up until your chin is over the bar.
Lower slowly all the way to straight arms.
When all sets reach the top of your rep range, add weight with a dip belt or a dumbbell between your feet.
breathing: Breathe out as you pull up, in as you lower.
feelItIn: The sides of your back and your biceps.
commonMistakes: Chin poking forward to 'reach' the bar

name: Chin-up
purpose: A pull-up with palms facing you: usually a little easier and works the biceps harder.
cue: Palms toward you, pull your chest to the bar.
setup: Grab the bar with palms facing you, about shoulder-width.
Hang with arms straight.
execution: Pull your shoulders down, then pull until your chin is over the bar.
Lower slowly to straight arms.
breathing: Breathe out as you pull up, in as you lower.
feelItIn: Your back and biceps.
commonMistakes: Not straightening the arms at the bottom

name: Standing calf raise
purpose: Builds the calf muscles of your lower legs, which also helps your cycling.
cue: Full stretch at the bottom, pause high on your toes.
setup: Stand on the machine's step with the balls of your feet on the edge and shoulders under the pads.
Let your heels hang down. No machine? Hold a dumbbell and use a step.
execution: Rise up onto your toes as high as you can.
Pause for a second at the top.
Lower slowly until you feel a deep stretch in your calves.
breathing: Breathe out going up, in going down.
feelItIn: Your calves.

name: Seated calf raise
purpose: Works the deeper calf muscle, which shows up best with bent knees.
cue: Slow stretch down, pause at the top.
setup: Sit at the machine with the balls of your feet on the step and the pad on your lower thighs.
Release the safety lever.
execution: Lower your heels as far as they go.
Rise up onto your toes and pause.
Lower slowly. Re-engage the lever at the end.
breathing: Breathe out going up, in going down.
feelItIn: Lower and deeper in your calves.

name: Calf press on the leg press
purpose: A calf exercise using the leg press, handy when the calf machine is taken.
cue: Balls of the feet on the edge, push with your toes only.
setup: Sit in the leg press with your legs straight (knees soft) and only the balls of your feet on the bottom edge of the platform.
Keep the safety catches engaged if your machine allows it.
execution: Push the platform away by pointing your toes.
Let it come back slowly for a deep calf stretch.
breathing: Breathe out as you push, in as you return.
feelItIn: Your calves.
safety: Keep your feet firmly on the platform; go lighter than you think.

name: Rear delt fly
purpose: Builds the back of your shoulders for a rounder, more balanced look and healthier shoulders.
cue: Arms wide like wings, lead with the elbows, light weight.
setup: Sit on the end of a bench, lean forward with your chest near your knees.
Hold light dumbbells hanging under your legs, palms facing each other.
execution: Lift the dumbbells out to the sides with slightly bent elbows until your arms are level with your body.
Pause, then lower slowly.
breathing: Breathe out as you lift, in as you lower.
feelItIn: The back of your shoulders.

name: Reverse pec deck
purpose: A machine version of the rear delt fly; very easy to feel the right muscle.
cue: Chest on the pad, sweep your arms back, squeeze.
setup: Set the machine handles to the rear position. Sit facing the pad.
Adjust the seat so the handles are at shoulder height.
execution: Push the handles back and out in an arc until your arms are in line with your body.
Pause, then return slowly.
breathing: Breathe out as you push back, in as you return.
feelItIn: The back of your shoulders.

name: Barbell curl
purpose: Builds the biceps with a bar, so you can use a bit more weight than with dumbbells.
cue: Elbows still, curl the bar up, lower slowly.
setup: Stand tall holding a barbell (or EZ-bar) with palms up, hands shoulder-width.
execution: Curl the bar up toward your shoulders, keeping your elbows by your sides.
Squeeze, then lower slowly until your arms are straight.
breathing: Breathe out as you curl, in as you lower.
feelItIn: The front of your upper arms.
safety: Fixed-weight or EZ bars are fine: log the total weight you lift.

name: Machine preacher curl
purpose: A biceps curl with your arms resting on a pad, so you can't cheat.
cue: Arms flat on the pad, curl up, lower all the way.
setup: Adjust the seat so your armpits are snug against the top of the pad.
Grip the handles with palms up.
execution: Curl the handles up toward your shoulders.
Lower slowly until your arms are nearly straight.
breathing: Breathe out as you curl, in as you lower.
feelItIn: The front of your upper arms.
commonMistakes: Lifting the elbows off the pad

name: Hanging knee raise
purpose: Strengthens your lower stomach and grip by lifting your knees while hanging from a bar.
cue: Curl your hips up, no swinging.
setup: Hang from a pull-up bar with straight arms (or use the arm pads of a captain's chair).
execution: Lift your knees toward your chest, curling your hips up at the top.
Lower your legs slowly until they're straight down. Stop any swing before the next rep.
breathing: Breathe out as you lift, in as you lower.
feelItIn: Your lower stomach.
commonMistakes: Only lifting the knees without curling the hips

name: Hanging leg raise
purpose: A harder version of the knee raise with straighter legs.
cue: Legs nearly straight, lift with control, no swinging.
setup: Hang from a pull-up bar with straight arms.
execution: Keeping your legs nearly straight, lift them until they're level with your hips or higher.
Lower slowly.
breathing: Breathe out as you lift, in as you lower.
feelItIn: Your whole stomach, especially the lower part.
commonMistakes: Bending the knees a lot when tired

name: Ab wheel rollout
purpose: A tough core exercise: rolling out and back makes your stomach fight to keep your back from sagging.
cue: Tuck your bum, roll out slowly, pull back with your stomach.
setup: Kneel on a mat holding an ab wheel (or a barbell with round plates) under your shoulders.
execution: Tighten your stomach and tuck your hips slightly.
Roll forward as far as you can without your lower back sagging.
Pull back to the start using your stomach.
breathing: Breathe in as you roll out, out as you come back.
feelItIn: Your whole stomach.
commonMistakes: Rolling out too far too soon
Pushing the hips back to return

name: Cable crunch
purpose: A crunch with cable weight, so your stomach muscles can get stronger over time.
cue: Curl your ribs toward your hips; the hips stay still.
setup: Attach a rope to a high cable. Kneel facing the machine holding the rope beside your head.
execution: Curl your chest down toward your knees by rounding your spine.
Squeeze your stomach, then return slowly.
breathing: Breathe out as you crunch, in as you return.
feelItIn: The front of your stomach.
commonMistakes: Sitting the hips back instead of curling

name: Incline barbell bench press
purpose: Builds the upper chest and front shoulders with a barbell, so you can load it heavier than dumbbells.
cue: Low incline, bar to upper chest, shoulder blades pinned.
setup: Set an incline bench (about 30°) in a rack, or use an incline bench station. Set the safeties.
Lie back with your eyes under the bar, grip a little wider than shoulder-width.
execution: Unrack, lower the bar to your upper chest under control.
Press it back up over your shoulders.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower the weight, breathe out as you push or pull it.
feelItIn: Your upper chest and shoulders.
safety: Use safety arms or a spotter.

name: Bulgarian split squat
purpose: A split squat with the back foot up on a bench: hard, but one of the best builders for legs and glutes.
cue: Back foot on the bench, drop straight down, front foot flat.
setup: Stand about two steps in front of a bench, facing away from it.
Put the top of one foot on the bench behind you. Hold dumbbells by your sides (or nothing to start).
execution: Lower your back knee toward the floor, keeping your front foot flat.
Go down until your front thigh is about level with the floor.
Push through your front foot to stand up. Do all reps, then switch legs.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower the weight, breathe out as you push or pull it.
feelItIn: The front leg's thigh and glute; a stretch in the back leg's hip.
commonMistakes: Front foot too close to the bench

name: Barbell hip thrust
purpose: The most direct glute builder: strong glutes power your squats, deadlifts and cycling.
cue: Chin tucked, ribs down, drive your hips up and squeeze hard.
setup: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench, a padded barbell across your hips.
Bend your knees so your feet are flat, about hip-width apart.
execution: Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your body is flat from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes hard for a second at the top.
Lower your hips under control.
breathing: Breathe in at the bottom, out as you push up.
feelItIn: Your glutes, strongly.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back at the top
Feet too far away (hamstrings take over)
safety: Use a bar pad or a folded mat. Start with just the bar.

name: Dumbbell lateral raise
purpose: Builds the side of your shoulders, which makes your shoulders look broader.
cue: Lead with the elbows, lift out to shoulder height, light weight.
setup: Stand tall holding light dumbbells by your sides, palms facing in.
execution: Raise your arms out to the sides with a slight bend in the elbows, until they're level with your shoulders.
Pause, then lower slowly.
breathing: Breathe out as you lift, in as you lower.
feelItIn: The outside of your shoulders.

name: Cable lateral raise
purpose: A lateral raise with a cable, which keeps tension on the shoulder through the whole movement.
cue: Pull out and up in a wide arc to shoulder height.
setup: Set a handle at the bottom of a cable. Stand side-on and hold it with the hand farther from the machine.
execution: Raise the handle out to the side until your arm is level with your shoulder.
Lower slowly. Do all reps, then switch sides.
breathing: Breathe out as you lift, in as you lower.
feelItIn: The outside of your shoulder.

name: Hammer curl
purpose: A curl with palms facing each other: builds the biceps plus the forearm muscle that makes arms look thicker.
cue: Thumbs up, elbows still, curl and lower slowly.
setup: Stand tall with dumbbells by your sides, palms facing your legs.
execution: Curl the dumbbells up keeping your thumbs pointing up.
Lower slowly to straight arms.
breathing: Breathe out as you curl, in as you lower.
feelItIn: The front of your upper arm and the top of your forearm.

name: Overhead cable triceps extension
purpose: Works the long part of the triceps with a big stretch; great for arm size.
cue: Elbows pointing forward, straighten your arms overhead.
setup: Attach a rope to a cable at about chest height. Face away from the machine, holding the rope behind your head.
Step forward into a split stance and lean slightly forward, elbows by your head.
execution: Straighten your arms forward and up until they're fully extended.
Bend your elbows slowly to bring the rope back behind your head.
breathing: Breathe out as you extend, in as you return.
feelItIn: The back of your upper arms, with a stretch near the armpit.
commonMistakes: Moving the shoulders instead of the elbows

name: Dip
purpose: Lowering and pushing your body up between parallel bars: builds chest, triceps and shoulders.
cue: Lean slightly forward, lower to shoulder level with elbows, push up.
setup: Grab the parallel bars and jump or step up to straight arms.
Lean slightly forward, knees bent.
execution: Lower yourself by bending your elbows until your shoulders are about level with your elbows.
Push back up to straight arms.
When all sets reach the top of the range, add weight with a dip belt.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower, out as you push up.
feelItIn: The back of your arms and the lower chest.
commonMistakes: Going so deep the shoulders hurt
safety: If dips hurt your shoulders, stop and use the assisted version or push-ups instead.

name: Assisted dip machine
purpose: A dip with help from a machine so you can build up to bodyweight dips.
cue: Chest up, lower until your elbows are at 90°, push up.
setup: Choose the amount of help (more weight = more help). Kneel or stand on the pad and grab the dip handles.
execution: Lower yourself until your elbows are bent about 90°.
Push back up to straight arms.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower, out as you push.
feelItIn: The back of your arms and the chest.
safety: On the machine, the number is help, so a lower number means you're stronger.

name: Leg extension
purpose: Isolates the front of your thighs; good extra quad work with no back load.
cue: Kick up until your legs are straight, squeeze, lower slowly.
setup: Adjust the seat so your knees line up with the machine's pivot and the pad sits on your lower shins.
execution: Straighten your legs until they're fully extended.
Squeeze for a second, then lower slowly.
breathing: Breathe out as you extend, in as you lower.
feelItIn: The front of your thighs.

name: Hack squat machine
purpose: A machine squat on an angled sled: lets you train your legs hard with your back supported.
cue: Back flat on the pad, sit deep, drive up through your whole foot.
setup: Stand on the platform with your back against the pad and shoulders under the pads.
Feet shoulder-width in the middle of the platform. Release the safety handles.
execution: Lower by bending your knees until your thighs are about level with the platform or lower.
Push back up until your legs are nearly straight.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower the weight, breathe out as you push or pull it.
feelItIn: The front of your thighs and glutes.
safety: Re-engage the safety handles before stepping out.

name: Walking lunge
purpose: Lunging forward step after step: builds legs, glutes and balance.
cue: Long step, drop the back knee, push through the front heel.
setup: Stand tall with dumbbells by your sides (or none) with space to walk.
execution: Take a long step forward and lower your back knee toward the floor.
Push through your front foot and bring the back leg through into the next step.
Each leg counts as one rep.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower the weight, breathe out as you push or pull it.
feelItIn: The thighs and glutes.

name: Reverse lunge
purpose: A lunge stepping backward: friendlier on the knees than a forward lunge.
cue: Step back, drop the back knee, push through the front foot.
setup: Stand tall with dumbbells by your sides (or none).
execution: Step one foot back and lower your back knee toward the floor.
Push through your front foot to return to standing. Alternate legs or do one side at a time.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower the weight, breathe out as you push or pull it.
feelItIn: The front leg's thigh and glute.

name: Pec deck
purpose: A machine chest fly that works the chest without the triceps.
cue: Hug a big tree, squeeze your chest, return slowly.
setup: Adjust the seat so the handles are at chest height. Sit tall with your back on the pad.
execution: Bring the handles together in front of your chest in a wide arc.
Squeeze, then open slowly until you feel a chest stretch.
breathing: Breathe out as you squeeze, in as you open.
feelItIn: Across your chest.
commonMistakes: Letting the arms go too far back

name: Cable fly
purpose: Chest fly with cables, keeping constant tension; good for the upper chest when done low to high.
cue: Slight bend in the elbows, sweep your hands together.
setup: Set both cable handles at shoulder height (or low for an upper-chest focus). Stand in the middle with a handle in each hand, one foot forward.
execution: With a slight bend in your elbows, bring your hands together in front of your chest.
Open slowly until you feel a chest stretch.
breathing: Breathe out as you bring the hands together, in as you open.
feelItIn: Across your chest.
commonMistakes: Turning it into a press by bending the elbows a lot

name: Push-up
purpose: The classic bodyweight press for chest, shoulders and arms. Works anywhere.
cue: Body in a straight line, chest to the floor, push it away.
setup: Put your hands on the floor a bit wider than your shoulders, legs straight behind you.
Squeeze your glutes and stomach so your body is a straight line.
execution: Lower your chest toward the floor, elbows at about 45°.
Push back up to straight arms.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower, out as you push.
feelItIn: Your chest and the back of your arms.

name: Incline push-up
purpose: A push-up with your hands on a bench or bar: easier, so you can learn good form.
cue: Hands on the bench, straight body, chest to the edge.
setup: Put your hands on a bench or a racked barbell, a bit wider than your shoulders. Walk your feet back until your body is straight.
execution: Lower your chest to the bench.
Push back up. The lower the bench, the harder it gets.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower, out as you push.
feelItIn: Your chest and arms.

name: Close-grip bench press
purpose: A bench press with hands closer together: builds triceps and helps your regular bench.
cue: Hands shoulder-width, elbows tucked, bar to lower chest.
setup: Set up like a normal bench press (safeties set!), but grip the bar about shoulder-width.
execution: Lower the bar to your lower chest with elbows close to your sides.
Press back up.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower the weight, breathe out as you push or pull it.
feelItIn: The back of your arms and your chest.
safety: Use safety arms or a spotter.

name: Skull crusher (EZ bar)
purpose: A lying triceps exercise that builds arm size; the name sounds worse than it is.
cue: Upper arms still, lower the bar to your forehead, extend.
setup: Lie on a flat bench holding an EZ-bar (or dumbbells) above your chest with arms straight.
execution: Bend your elbows to lower the bar toward your forehead, keeping your upper arms still.
Straighten your arms back up.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower, out as you extend.
feelItIn: The back of your upper arms.
safety: Start light and move slowly. Lowering slightly behind your head is easier on the elbows.

name: Incline dumbbell curl
purpose: A curl on an incline bench that stretches the biceps for extra growth.
cue: Arms hanging back, curl without moving your elbows.
setup: Set a bench to about 45° and sit back with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging straight down.
execution: Curl the dumbbells up, keeping your upper arms still.
Lower slowly to a full stretch.
breathing: Breathe out as you curl, in as you lower.
feelItIn: The front of your upper arms, with a big stretch at the bottom.
commonMistakes: Lifting the shoulders off the bench

name: Glute bridge
purpose: A beginner-friendly glute exercise lying on the floor; teaches you to use your glutes.
cue: Heels down, push your hips up, squeeze.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart.
execution: Push through your heels and lift your hips until your body is straight from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes for two seconds, then lower.
breathing: Breathe out as you lift, in as you lower.
feelItIn: Your glutes.

name: Straight-arm pulldown
purpose: Isolates your lats with straight arms; great for learning to feel your back working.
cue: Arms long, sweep the bar down to your thighs.
setup: Attach a straight bar to a high cable. Stand facing it, step back and hinge forward slightly, arms straight and up.
execution: Keeping your arms straight, pull the bar down in an arc to your thighs.
Return slowly until your arms are overhead.
breathing: Breathe out as you pull down, in as you return.
feelItIn: Under your armpits and down the sides of your back.

name: Bodyweight box squat
purpose: Squatting down to a bench with no weight: the very first step to learning a squat.
cue: Arms forward for balance, sit back to touch the bench, stand up.
setup: Stand in front of a bench, feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out.
Reach your arms forward for balance.
execution: Sit back and down until your bum lightly touches the bench.
Stand back up, pushing through your whole foot.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower the weight, breathe out as you push or pull it.
feelItIn: The front of your thighs and your glutes.

name: Inverted row
purpose: Rowing your body up to a low bar: a bodyweight back exercise that builds toward pull-ups.
cue: Body straight like a plank, pull your chest to the bar.
setup: Set a bar in a rack at about waist height. Lie under it and grab it a bit wider than shoulder-width.
Straighten your body with heels on the floor.
execution: Pull your chest to the bar, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower slowly to straight arms. Bend your knees to make it easier.
breathing: Breathe out as you pull, in as you lower.
feelItIn: Your upper back.

name: Front squat
purpose: A squat with the bar on the front of your shoulders: very upright and great for the quads and core.
cue: Elbows high, chest tall, sit straight down.
setup: Set the bar in the rack at shoulder height with the safeties below your bottom position.
Step in so the bar rests on the front of your shoulders. Fingertips under the bar, elbows high.
execution: Brace and sit straight down between your heels, keeping your elbows high.
Go as deep as you can with a flat back, then drive up.
breathing: Take a deep breath into your belly and tighten your stomach as if bracing for a poke, then hold it through the hard part of the rep. Breathe out at the top.
feelItIn: The front of your thighs, and your upper back holding the bar.
commonMistakes: Elbows dropping so the bar rolls forward
safety: Squat inside the rack with the safety pins set. To bail, push the bar forward and step back.

name: Lying leg curl
purpose: Strengthens the back of your thighs while lying face down.
cue: Hips pressed into the pad, curl your heels to your bum.
setup: Lie face down with your knees just off the end of the pad and the roller above your heels.
execution: Curl your heels toward your bum.
Lower slowly until your legs are nearly straight.
breathing: Breathe out as you curl, in as you lower.
feelItIn: The back of your thighs.

name: Machine row
purpose: A chest-supported rowing machine: easy to learn and easy on the lower back.
cue: Chest on the pad, pull your elbows back, squeeze.
setup: Adjust the seat so the handles are at chest height and your chest rests on the pad.
execution: Pull the handles back, driving your elbows behind you.
Squeeze your shoulder blades, then return slowly.
breathing: Breathe out as you pull, in as you return.
feelItIn: Your upper back.

name: Bird dog
purpose: A gentle core and back exercise on hands and knees; teaches you to keep your spine still.
cue: Reach long, opposite arm and leg, hips stay level.
setup: Get on your hands and knees, hands under shoulders and knees under hips. Back flat.
execution: Slowly reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are level with your body.
Hold for two seconds without letting your hips tilt.
Return and switch sides. Each side counts as one rep.
breathing: Breathe out as you reach, in as you return.
feelItIn: Your stomach, lower back and glutes, gently.

name: Suitcase carry
purpose: Carrying one heavy dumbbell on one side: your core has to work hard to keep you upright.
cue: Stand perfectly tall; don't lean toward or away from the weight.
setup: Put a heavy dumbbell beside one foot. Squat down, grab it and stand tall.
execution: Walk with short steady steps, staying perfectly upright.
Walk for the target time, then switch hands.
breathing: Breathe steadily.
feelItIn: The side of your waist opposite the weight, and your grip.

name: Negative pull-up
purpose: Jump or step up to the top of a pull-up and lower yourself as slowly as you can. Builds pull-up strength fast.
cue: Start at the top, take 3–5 seconds to lower all the way.
setup: Stand on a box or bench under a pull-up bar. Grab the bar a bit wider than your shoulders.
execution: Jump or step up so your chin is over the bar.
Lower yourself slowly, taking 3–5 seconds, until your arms are straight.
Step back up and repeat.
breathing: Breathe steadily as you lower.
feelItIn: The sides of your back and your biceps.
commonMistakes: Not reaching straight arms at the bottom

name: Kneeling plank
purpose: An easier plank on your knees: the first step to a full plank.
cue: Straight line from head to knees, squeeze your glutes.
setup: Lie face down, prop up on your forearms with elbows under shoulders.
Keep your knees on the floor.
execution: Lift your hips so your body is straight from head to knees.
Hold, breathing slowly.
breathing: Breathe slowly; don't hold your breath.
feelItIn: Your stomach.
